sequentialSelection.label: Public power, diversity and belief
sequentialSelection.concept: Study how authority, law, social belonging and cultural representation shape public life. Political philosophy, human rights and constitutional comparison are combined with social theory, media and racialisation, radicalisation prevention and peacebuilding. World myth, ancient civic religion and Mediterranean cultural exchange provide concrete belief-related study, while qualitative, historical and empirical research supports independent inquiry. This is a broader response to the confirmed political-cultural-religious core; it does not reproduce Abrahamic history, scriptural exegesis or Muhammad studies.

sequentialSelection.label: Myth, media and cultural meaning
sequentialSelection.concept: Study how narratives, visual and material culture, media and philosophical ideas create meaning and shape authority. Comparative world myth, Western and African religious art, Mediterranean exchange and ancient civic religion anchor a cultural inquiry developed through film, documentary, literary interpretation and critical media research. Philosophical study of God, ethics, self and agency complements it. No continuous comparative mysticism, Abrahamic traditions, Bible/Quran commentary or specialist religious education is promised.

sequentialSelection.label: Empires, cultural encounters and conflict
sequentialSelection.concept: Study how empires, colonialism, states and cultural encounters shape identities, conflict and social boundaries. Modern and imperial history, Indigenous histories, international/comparative politics and peacebuilding combine with social theory, racialised media and tangible myth/religion/material-culture cases. Qualitative, statistical, documentary and historical research develop comparative inquiry. This offers a global historical response, without claiming sustained Middle Eastern history, Arabic or the excluded Utrecht specialisation.
